title: Chapter 2 Quiz 4
description: Top-down, bottom-up, and other ways to classify algorithms.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which design approach breaks a complex problem into simpler sub-problems?
questions.explanation: The top-down approach decomposes a problem until elementary solutions are reached.

questions.question: The bottom-up approach first solves the simplest sub-problems, then combines them to solve the whole problem.
questions.explanation: Bottom-up works from the small pieces up to the full solution.

questions.question: In the {{1}} approach a problem is broken down into smaller parts, and in the {{2}} approach the simplest sub-problems are solved first.
Match each classification to what it describes.
right: Uses random choices to speed up the solution
Compares algorithms by execution time, such as O(n)
Groups algorithms by field, such as artificial intelligence
Explores a large space of possible solutions
questions.explanation: These are the 'other classifications' presented in the course.

questions.question: Which of these factors help us **choose** an algorithm?
options: Whether an exact or approximate solution is needed
questions.explanation: Algorithms are chosen according to efficiency, the nature of the problem, hardware constraints and the guarantee of the solution.

questions.question: Randomized quicksort is an example of…
questions.explanation: It picks random choices to speed up the resolution.

questions.question: Which classification lets us compare algorithms by their execution time, for example O(n) or exponential?
questions.explanation: Complexity analysis compares the theoretical efficiency of algorithms.
